Title: First 5 minutes
Tagline: Grab what disappears first, then look around
When: You just arrived at a machine and do not know yet what is wrong. This takes the volatile data (connections, processes, sessions) before it changes, saves a snapshot, and runs the Live Hunt.

Title: Suspected malware
Tagline: Unknown program, alert from antivirus or EDR, odd behaviour
When: Something is running that should not be, or an alert named a file. Collects process, service, task and autostart state, execution traces (Prefetch, Amcache, Shimcache), Defender history and the logs that show what ran.

Title: Suspicious logons or RDP
Tagline: Brute force, a stranger logged in, lateral movement
When: Someone may have logged on who should not have, or an account is being guessed. Collects sessions, accounts, the RDP traces left on this machine and the logon, RDP and remote-access logs.

Title: Ransomware or destructive activity
Tagline: Files encrypted, backups deleted, services stopped
When: Files are encrypted or shadow copies are gone. Capture memory FIRST if the machine is still on (Memory page): keys and the running malware may still be there. This set collects state, shares, recent dropped files and the logs around the event.

Title: Data theft or user activity
Tagline: What did this user open, copy, browse or plug in
When: Looking at what a person did: files opened, USB and shares, browser history, deleted files. Several of these items hold private data; use them only with authority.

Title: Persistence sweep
Tagline: How would an attacker come back after a reboot
When: Checks every common autostart place and scores it: services, tasks, Run keys, startup folders, WMI, drivers and registry hooks.

Title: Full triage
Tagline: Everything that is safe to collect live
When: You want it all and have the time and disk space. Runs all live-response tasks, all triage tasks, all file artifacts except raw disk structures, every event log that exists, a snapshot and the Live Hunt.
